title: Nadeem Ahmad v. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitarana Nigam, Varanasi
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ disposed without merits; liberty to object under para 6.8 with stay of coercive action.
headnote: Allahabad High Court disposed of a consumer writ seeking mandamus to decide a representation under clause 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, without expressing any opinion on merits. Liberty was given to file an objection under para 6.8 within four weeks, to be decided after hearing within four weeks thereafter, with coercive recovery stayed for eight weeks or until disposal of the objection, whichever is earlier.
facts: Nadeem Ahmad, a consumer of Purvanchal Vidhut Vitarana Nigam at Varanasi, filed a writ petition seeking a mandamus that respondent no. 2 decide his representation dated 20 May 2022 strictly in accordance with clause 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petition was directed against an impugned electricity demand. Counsel for the distribution licensee stated on instructions that the petitioner may file an objection against that demand, which would be decided in accordance with law within a time-bound period.

holding_units.topic: objection to assessment as alternate remedy
holding_units.holding: Without expressing any opinion on merits, a writ seeking mandamus to decide a representation under clause 8.1 was disposed of by giving liberty to the consumer to submit an objection under para 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within four weeks. If so submitted, respondent no. 2 shall decide it in accordance with law, preferably within four weeks, after affording a reasonable opportunity of hearing. Coercive action on the impugned demand is stayed for eight weeks or until disposal of the objection, whichever is earlier.

principle_tags.application: Writ seeking a clause 8.1 decision on a representation was disposed without merits, relegating the consumer to a para 6.8 objection against the impugned demand.
If the para 6.8 objection is filed within four weeks, it is to be decided after hearing within four weeks, and coercive recovery is stayed for eight weeks or until disposal, whichever is earlier.

not_decided.point: Merits of the impugned demand and of the representation dated 20.05.2022
not_decided.note: Court expressly declined to express any opinion on merits.

not_decided.point: Whether the demand is governed by clause 8.1 (theft) or para 6.8 (unauthorised use)
not_decided.note: Petitioner invoked clause 8.1; the Court directed a para 6.8 objection without resolving the characterisation.
